issue.title: test_new_process_loads_remembered_admin_center_section fails under the full parallel lane, passes in isolation
issue.description:
FOUND BY the sase-xz.land agent while consuming `just check-full` monitor 4fvbspmpxjw5
(landing gate for epic sase-xz, file-aware pager syntax highlighting). Every lint gate,
SASE validation, committed plans, and the whole `just test-cost` full suite passed; the
only failing step was the last one, `just selection-health --fail-on-new-flake`, which
promoted this node with no entry in tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt.

NOT caused by epic sase-xz. The node's oldest promoting record predates every sase-xz
commit (a45669b26 "fix(agent): preserve monitor fork context", committed 2026-09-06
14:33, versus the epic's first landed commit a9f95ca5e on 2026-09-07 14:10), and the
test exercises the ACE admin-center tab-resume path, which the pager epic never touches.

`just selection-health --fail-on-new-flake` is the last gate of `just check-full`, so an
undeclared node here blocks every landing agent that reaches it. This bead is filed so
the node can carry a baseline entry with a named owner.

The test opens two successive AcePage instances: the first presses `#`, switches the
Config Center to the Procs tab, escapes, and asserts `app._last_admin_center_tab ==
"procs"`; the second asserts a fresh app instance reloads that remembered tab from the
persisted admin-center tab history and shows the "resume Procs" home hint. Root cause is
not proven. It is the same shape as the flake class epic sase-j7 owns (process-global /
persisted state leaking between tests under the full parallel lane) and as sase-md, whose
config-center state `os.replace` isolation fix already retired an earlier
test_config_center_state node.

task_type_fields.evidence:
Five eligible full-lane records (schema 2, at most 5 failures each) across three
unrelated heads, with later full runs passing the node:

1. 20260906T205004Z-a45669b26fd3-2039637-full-run.json (head a45669b26 "fix(agent):
   preserve monitor fork context", dirty, 12 changed files, 2 failures) - predates the
   sase-xz epic entirely.
2. 20260907T135748Z-e2ce985dd5b0-3949628-full-run.json (head e2ce985dd "fix(bead): give
   targeted cleanup paths a real owner lookup", dirty, 2 changed files, 3 failures).
3. 20260907T184446Z-a9f95ca5e645-503393-full-run.json (clean tree, 2 failures).
4. 20260907T185026Z-a9f95ca5e645-642293-full-run.json (dirty, 11 changed files, 2
   failures).
5. 20260907T185118Z-a9f95ca5e645-672260-full-run.json (clean tree, sole failure).

Records 3-5 come from workspace sase_12, not from the landing workspace, and the node's
co-failures differ in every record (models-panel runner limit, procs-pane navigation,
plugins-catalog scale fixture), so nothing links them to one change set.

Fail rate: parallel full lane only. Serial isolated rerun on the sase-xz landing tree
passed (`.venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:randomly -q
tests/ace/tui/test_config_center_resume.py::test_new_process_loads_remembered_admin_center_section`
-> 1 passed, 3.16s call). The same tree's `just test-cost` full-suite lane also passed
the node. No serial reproduction of the failure.

payload.description: sase-j7 owns the process-global/persisted-state flake class this full-parallel-lane-only node most resembles
